acceptance.KA6-T01: Controller and turn orchestrator pass original requests without route injection, seeding an execution preference, semantic classification or helper dispatch; four message scenarios observe zero classifier/tool calls.
acceptance.KA6-T02: All 24 legacy policy/outcome combinations allow answering without calling or declining; exact user names/aliases remain correctly represented. Optional voluntary audit does not grant execution rights.
acceptance.KA6-T03: Skill loading remains explicit and returns resources. Agent-loop mixed requests continue through generic evidence after the first tool; no host task finalization follows from a query.
acceptance.KA6-T04: Unused, failed, missing and denied optional capability scenarios all retain generic tool execution and further model turns. A permanent missing dependency uses the native nonretryable error contract; ordinary safe transient transport retry behavior was preserved.
acceptance.KA6-T05: Target/compatibility filtering and actual permission/read-only execution gates remain unchanged and their regression packages pass. No package manager, Docker installation path or repair is selected by the new controller code.

findings: Legacy tests required primary-group collapse, forced call/decline, semantic user classification or require policies.
New fixture initially used an internal gate field instead of the public SetGate interface.
Tests assert unchanged requests, composable discovery, exact user references and preserved audit state instead of preference gates.
Permanent dependency failure fixture uses RetryableToolError=false; it no longer models a transient transport error.
Four Go packages plus dedicated controller scenarios pass.

scopeNotes: The legacy CheckFinalGate function was not in the baseline main Agent finalization path. It is now inert for compatibility; the active automatic route prompt injection was removed.
Mock providers establish host control flow, not live model reasoning quality. KA9 still requires real model evaluation.
Real operation verification, Target authorization, protection, lifecycle and redaction remain separate KA7 acceptance; capability metadata is not an authority source.
Optional packaged-snapshot/native opt-in tests are not counted as passed here; candidate/source compatibility belongs to KA10.
